voice_description: Role: extremely old storybook witch with a highly shaped animated character voice. Gender: female. Age: around ninety years old, physically aged but mentally sharp. Persistent vocal posture: narrow forward mouth position with tight nasal resonance and a dry, lightly constricted throat throughout the entire performance. Pitch: thin upper-mid register with unstable little rises, downward cracks and occasional unexpectedly low creaky notes. Resonance: strongly forward and nasal with very little chest resonance. Timbre: papery, brittle, reedy, scratchy, dry, creaky and slightly wheezing. Phonation: irregular aged vocal-fold closure with vocal fry, tiny voice cracks and occasional quavering. Breathing: small audible inhales, dry little huffs and occasional amused breathy chuckles between thoughts. Articulation: sharp consonants, stretched crooked vowels and peculiar emphasis on interesting words. Prosody: highly irregular rhythm with sly pauses, quick bursts and strange melodic turns. Personality: clever, eccentric, mischievous, suspicious and delighted by dangerous magic. Important: this must sound like a deliberately performed classic animated witch character, not merely an elderly woman reading dialogue. Maintain the crooked, reedy, creaky vocal posture through every sentence.
direction: Use sly conversational amusement with little dry chuckles, creaky pitch changes and tiny suspicious pauses. Allow a brief breathy 'heh' or amused vocal catch naturally between phrases, but keep the speech intelligible.

text: Heh... there you are. I wondered how long it would take you to find my cottage. Come in, come in. The kettle is warm, the ravens are behaving terribly, and something in my cupboard has been whispering your name since midnight.
